response.rationale: “Sahabat karib” and “kawan baik” are ordinary ways to express a particularly close or best friend in Indonesian and Malaysian Malay, respectively. The contrast is useful without implying exclusive ownership.
response.risk_rationale: “Kawan baik” can occasionally mean simply a good friend rather than one’s closest friend, depending on context.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Sahabat baik” may be understood in both varieties, but Indonesian commonly favors “sahabat karib” while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “kawan baik” in everyday contexts.
